text:
Mike: heads-up — canary run on awq weight-only (gpt2-like) shows 5-8% p99 increase vs baseline after the recent pack-prefetch tweak. Not huge but consistent across multiple shards. Any ideas? :thinking_face:
Anya: ugh. saw similar on a handful of jobs this morning. looks correlated with small-group sizes (g=16/32) and high prefix reuse. Might be prefetch / slab alignment causing extra memcpy?
Jiayi: can you paste the profiler output? curious about kernel vs memcpy time.
Mike: pasted a short trace: ```
# trace summary (canary-2026-03-14)
kernel_forward    1123ms
kv_prefetch       152ms
memcpy_pack        78ms
pack_overhead      96ms
other               9ms
```
Mike: note baseline had kv_prefetch ~80ms and memcpy_pack ~40ms.
Surya: interesting — pack_overhead jumped. Did the packer switch to the new stride-aware path? That path trades a bit more CPU to reduce cache misses, maybe not worth it for small groups.
Anya: yeah the recent change enabled stride heuristics by default for awq weight-only. We added a prefetch that walks the slab in 64B steps. Works great for big groups but could thrash for g<=32.
Jiayi: @perf-bot can you run microbench: pack_stride_off vs on for g=8/16/32, seq_len=32/128, with kv cache hit/miss cases?
perf-bot: queued bench job 3176543210-1: pack_stride_on/off microbench scheduled on perf-lab-3. Will post results when done. :robot_face:��
Anya: quick thought — kernel selection may also be falling back to slower int8 path for some layers after calibration heuristics changed. If we evict kv earlier due to prefetch, backend picks a smaller kernel variant (serial) -> p99 spike.
Mike: good call. On canary I saw more serial-pack kernel calls in the logs: `kernel_choice=serial_pack` vs baseline `vectorized_pack`
Jiayi: if it's kernel-choice related, we should capture a full debug trace for one request (kv indices, chosen kernel ids, batch shape). Mike can you attach one?
Mike: attached a tail of the debug log: ```
[2026-03-14T09:12:01Z] request id=abc123
layer=12 group=16 kernel=serial_pack latency=2.3ms
layer=13 group=16 kernel=vectorized_pack latency=0.7ms
kv_prefetch_hit=true prefetch_pages=3
```
Surya: that pattern (mix of serial+vectorized) often means heterogeneous group sizes or alignment mismatch causing pack to fallback layer-by-layer. The stride prefetch can change alignments so that some layers don't satisfy vectorized path alignment checks.
Anya: two action items: (1) run the microbench to quantify pack_stride impact, (2) instrument kernel-selector to log why it rejects vectorized path (alignment/stride/size) for each layer.
Jiayi: +1. Also we should rerun calibration for awq artifacts — calibration changes can alter group boundaries and quantized metadata, which interacts badly with the packer heuristics. Maybe revert default stride heuristic for awq until we validate.
Mike: I'll flip the feature flag for the canary and re-run. If p99 drops back to baseline we have a smoking gun.
perf-bot: bench results: pack_stride_on vs off (g in [8,16,32], seq=32):
- g=8: on=1.12ms/op, off=0.95ms/op
- g=16: on=1.05ms/op, off=0.97ms/op
- g=32: on=0.98ms/op, off=0.99ms/op
(prefetch enabled in both)
perf-bot: extra microbench with kv hit vs miss: pack_stride_on increases memcpy for small g when kv_hit=true.
Surya: bench aligns with hypothesis — stride pref on small groups is regressive. Also note it mitigates p99 for g>=32 a bit. So conditional enable by group-size probably best.
Anya: I'll open a PR to gate stride-prefetch to g>=32 for awq weight-only models, and add telemetry when selector rejects vectorized path.
Jiayi: also add an experiment flag to let packer fallback defer one layer and probe vectorized path once per request rather than permanently for that request — might reduce mixed-kernel churn.
Mike: thanks team. After PR I'll run canary again with feature flag off and with the new gated-on config. Will post numbers. :thumbsup:��
Surya: one more thing — check calibration outputs (scale/zero) for AWQ vs GPTQ. If calibration changes group boundaries we might need to pin group-size in the deployment to avoid mid-canary drift.
Mike: acknowledged. I'll snapshot calibration artifacts and pin during the canary.
perf-bot: note: rolled temp revert flag into canary at 3176543400 — warmup running. Will post perf summary at 3176543650.
Mike: thanks, closing the loop once we have the perf summary.
